summary: This is a reference page for the Snowflake-style SQL function H3_COVERAGE_STRINGS, which returns an ARRAY of VARCHAR hexadecimal IDs for the minimal set of H3 cells that completely cover a GEOGRAPHY shape at a given resolution. It gives the syntax, arguments (a GEOGRAPHY expression and an INTEGER resolution from 0 to 15), return type, a usage note that a cell is included if its boundary intersects the shape, and an example covering a San Francisco polygon at resolution 8. The surrounding navigation and boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Reference for the H3_COVERAGE_STRINGS SQL function, which returns hexadecimal H3 cell IDs covering a geography shape at a chosen resolution.
key_facts: H3_COVERAGE_STRINGS returns an ARRAY of hexadecimal IDs as VARCHAR values identifying H3 cells that completely cover a shape specified by a GEOGRAPHY object.
The target_resolution argument is an INTEGER between 0 and 15 (inclusive) specifying the H3 resolution of the returned H3 cells.
Specifying any INTEGER value outside the range 0 to 15 results in an error.
The function returns the hexadecimal IDs of the minimal set of H3 cells that completely cover the specified input shape.
Usage note: a cell is included in the result set if its boundary intersects the input shape.
The documented example applies H3_COVERAGE_STRINGS to a Polygon with vertices at approximately -122.48 longitude and 37.83 latitude, using resolution 8.
The example output for resolution 8 is an array of six cell IDs, beginning with "882830870bfffff" and including "8828308715fffff".
The example converts the text to a geography value using TO_GEGGRAPHY, as written in the note.
